brief.headline: Ricardo has lost 7.4% of his body weight in under 3 months and now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing, after an ED visit for dehydration and dizziness on Oct 9.

items.statement: Weight fell from 84.8 kg on Sep 5 to 78.5 kg on Nov 24, a loss of 6.3 kg (7.4%). The weights fell at each reading: 82.6 kg on Oct 1 and 80.4 kg on Oct 28. On Nov 24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten.
items.verifier_note: Weights, change (-6.3 kg, -7.4%), and the Nov 24 dietitian findings (poor appetite, skipped breakfast, ~50% of day center lunches) all match the vitals record and the note.

items.statement: On Oct 27 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting out of the tub. Ricardo said he has been skipping showers because he fears slipping. On Nov 4 the OT reassessed him as needing moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. He was independent at the last review.
items.verifier_note: The aide note (Oct 27) and OT note (Nov 4) support every detail, including independence at the last review.

items.statement: Ricardo went to the partner hospital ED on Oct 9 for dehydration and dizziness. He was treated and released the same day, with no new medications. On Oct 13 PCP follow-up he was back to baseline per his niece, and the plan was close monitoring for two weeks. Weight loss continued after this visit (80.4 kg on Oct 28, 78.5 kg on Nov 24).
items.verifier_note: The ED visit, same-day release, no new medications, back to baseline per niece, and two-week monitoring plan all match the notes. Weights of 80.4 kg and 78.5 kg match the vitals record, and both come after Oct 9.

items.statement: Several recommendations from Nov 4 and Nov 24 are open in the notes. The OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing. The dietitian planned an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems. The notes do not show whether any of these are in place.
items.verifier_note: The OT and dietitian recommendations are accurately listed. The cited notes contain no information on whether they were implemented, so the statement that this isn't shown is accurate.

questions_for_team: Who owns the follow-up on the weight loss, and what weight or intake trigger should prompt escalation beyond weekly weights?

Is there any link between the Oct 9 dehydration and dizziness, the poor appetite and weight loss, and the decline in bathing ability? Does the team want to review fluid intake and dizziness since the ED visit?
How quickly can the tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and added home care bathing hours be put in place? How will hygiene be covered while Ricardo is skipping showers?
Does the team want a fall-risk or home safety review, given his fear of slipping and need for hands-on help?
Does the active medication list match the intended simvastatin regimen? It currently shows both a 10 mg and a 20 mg tablet.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in that window, plus any discharge summaries from the window.
Falls and near-falls: check incident reports and notes for falls, fall-related injuries, or gait/balance concerns, given hip osteoarthritis and chronic back pain.

Medication changes in the window: reconcile the active list against prior list. Specifically review the new Simvastatin 10 MG start dated 2026-08-09 alongside the existing Simvastatin 20 MG entry (1998) for possible duplicate statin therapy, dose confusion, or an unrecorded dose change, and confirm who prescribed it and why.

Antiplatelet and cardiac regimen: confirm clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, and PRN nitroglycerin are still active and taken as prescribed; check for any bleeding, bruising, GI bleed signs, or Hgb/anemia labs, since he has anemia and is on clopidogrel.
Anemia and prediabetes labs: review CBC/hemoglobin and HbA1c or glucose results in the window and compare to prior values; note any new orders or results due.

Pain management: review chronic pain and low back pain scores, analgesic use (including topical hydrocortisone and any opioid or NSAID use not on the list), and any new pain-related complaints or requests.
Weight and BMI trend: obtain weights for the window versus prior baseline given obesity (BMI 30+) and related cardiometabolic risk; flag change of more than 5% or any unexplained change.
Blood pressure and heart rate: review readings in the window, especially with ischemic heart disease on metoprolol; flag hypotension, bradycardia, or chest pain reports and any nitroglycerin use.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: compare current ADL and IADL status (mobility, transfers, driving, medications, meals) with the last review; note any decline tied to hip OA or back pain.

Cognition, mood, and social: screen for any new cognitive concerns, depression or mood changes, sleep issues, and changes in attendance at PACE day center or missed appointments; review caregiver or family situation and any caregiver strain noted in the window. Also confirm the care-plan items due by 2026-11-30 (e.g., reassessment, goals review, advance directive status) and the allergy record (allergic disposition, reaction not documented; clarify specific allergens).
